To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the most efficient method of FIV purification is a combination of ultracentrifugations followed by immunoaffinity chromatography.
the FIV proteome can be analyzed using mass spectrometry after purification of viral particles by ultracentrifugion, sucrose gradient and/or subtilisin treatment.
the most reliable method for quantification of infectious FIV is the limiting dilution assay, and that the best method for purification of FIV is immunoaffinity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new methods for the purification of lentiviral preparations for use in immunological studies of lentiviral pathogenesis and for the development of lentiviral vaccines.
the development and application of methods for the detection and purification of FIV, and the characterization of the viral proteome, including host proteins incorporated into viral envelopes.
the development and application of methods for assessing feline retrovirus infection, infectivity, and purification.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
no single method is optimal for all assays.
there are many methods to purify lentiviruses.
the best purification method depends on the specific application.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
purification of FIV from cat plasma is feasible, but requires a combination of approaches to remove all contaminating proteins.
purification of viral preparations is a crucial step to ensure accurate quantification and analysis of the viral proteome.
FIV is a useful model for HIV, and that FIV is more easily purified than HIV.
The main takeaway from our work is that
purification of FIV is not necessary for detection of antibodies, viral RNA, viral DNA or viral proteins, or for detection of viral enzymes.
FIV preparations purified using ultracentrifugion and chromatography are suitable for a wide range of studies, including immune assays, and that purification does not affect infectivity.
the use of a combination of purification methods is necessary for a complete analysis of viral particles.
